452418.findings: Large half-leather bound volume (blue cloth boards, red leather spine and corners) of The Mercury, Hobart. First page shown reads 'The Mercury. Hobart: Friday Morning July 1, 1892. Price Twopence', so this looks like the July-December 1892 half-year run. Original Hobart newspaper, Tasmaniana, front page mostly classified advertisements. Content is digitised on Trove so research value is lower, but bound original volumes of 19th century Tasmanian papers have a collector and decorator market.
452418.condition: Boards scuffed and spotted, corners and spine leather worn and chipped, foxing and a damp/brown stain down the upper middle of the first page; internal completeness not shown.
452418.reason: Original bound 1892 Hobart Mercury half-year volume, Tasmaniana with a local collector market.
452418.marks_read: The Mercury, Hobart, Friday Morning July 1 1892, Price Twopence

452419.findings: Old paper-lined travelling trunk (interior papered with printed text and dot pattern, pink ribbon tie) holding about five antique dolls: at least three German-type bisque socket-head dolls with sleep eyes, open mouths showing teeth and real or mohair wigs (typical Armand Marseille / Schoenau and Hoffmeister type, c.1900-1920), one black-haired glazed china shoulder-head doll (c.1880-1910 type) in lace dress, plus a further doll in a white bonnet. Period cotton and lace clothes, leather or kid-type bodies visible on one. No head or neck marks photographed, so maker unconfirmed.
452419.condition: Clothing aged and soiled, wigs dry; bisque faces look intact in photos but no close-ups for hairlines; trunk worn and scuffed. Bodies and limbs not fully shown.
452419.reason: Group of antique German bisque and china head dolls in period trunk; antique doll collectors pay well per doll.

452420.condition: Glass appears intact; edges and mirror silvering look fair in photo.
452420.reason: Common mid-century etched swan mirror, low resale.

452421.findings: Six soda syphons in a blue painted wooden crate stencilled 'Property of Abbotts' (Tasmanian cordial maker). Syphons read: (1) clear 'The Property of Bradbury's Tasmania' with lady trade mark, 'never left on the shelf', red plastic head; (2) clear 'DCF Devonport Tas. Dixon' in triangle; (3) clear 'Dixon & Co Ltd Melbourne' lion trade mark 'Registered Trade Mark'; (4) cobalt blue etched '... Co ... Launceston' star device; (5) cobalt blue 'Abbotts ... Tasmania ... this syphon ... Abbott's' with medals/prize wording; (6) clear 'Crystal Cordial(?) ... CL' monogram, probably Launceston. Mostly Tasmanian makers, blue Tasmanian syphons are the most sought after.
452421.condition: Glass looks intact, some internal residue and staining; one chip-like flaw on base of blue Abbotts syphon possible; heads metal with wear, one plastic head; crate paint worn.
452421.reason: Six Tasmanian etched soda syphons incl. two cobalt blue, with branded Abbotts crate; strong local bottle collector market.
452421.marks_read: Property of Abbotts (crate); Bradbury's Tasmania; DCF Devonport Tas Dixon; Dixon & Co Melbourne; blue Launceston; blue Abbotts Tasmania; Crystal C L
